rv.q: Robert Hastie, in his final production as artistic director, shows his customary mastery in deploying a huge cast on the vast thrust stage of the Crucible.
Sheffield Theatres’ outgoing artistic director Robert Hastie allows the pace to flag significantly in parts, dwelling too long on each of the play’s many subplots
Chariots of Fire is a brilliantly staged show, demonstrating just why Robert Hastie is so well regarded.

cn.t: Mixed reception for this Olympic revival — visually impressive staging wins praise, but an overstretched script keeps it from gold. Energetic yet unfocused, it's a thoughtful if languid retelling that thrills in moments without fully hitting its stride.
